headline: Ministry of Independence Affairs Reveals India’s Freedom Was Originally Scheduled for a Tuesday
body:
The Ministry of Independence Affairs released a commemorative 800-page dossier today, revealing that India’s hard-fought sovereignty was technically slated for a Tuesday afternoon, but was delayed by two days due to a pending file clearance from a clerical officer in the British colonial archives.

According to the newly unearthed memorandum, the original proclamation was drafted on 100gsm parchment and featured a prominent typo that would have technically declared the country as the 'Republic of Uninterrupted Afternoon Naps.' The document remained trapped in an ink-stained mahogany drawer for forty-eight hours while a junior clerk waited for a fresh ribbon for his typewriter.

'It is truly a fascinating historical footnote,' said Dr. Ramesh Upadhyay, Chief Archivist of Trivial Records. 'If the clerk had possessed a functional stapler, the entire map of the subcontinent might have looked exactly the same, but we would all be required to wear hats on Wednesdays. It is a testament to our administrative resilience that we managed to become a nation despite the persistent shortage of typewriter ink in 1947.'
caption: History is written by the victors, but filed by the most confused clerks in the Empire. Turns out, freedom was just a ribbon-refill away! 🇮🇳📜 #IndiaAt79 #HistoryFacts #BureaucracyLife #IndependenceDay (satire)
